weaknesses: Career was in decline and the genuine swing of his peak years was not consistently available

name: Jaydev Unadkat
strengths: Experienced left-arm seamer with strong early IPL record and ability to take powerplay wickets with swing
weaknesses: Declining pace with age and batting is minimal contribution to team totals

name: AM Ghazanfar
strengths: Young Afghan leg-spinner who took 15 wickets in 2026 for MI with excellent deceptive variations
weaknesses: Very young with limited experience and quality batters can attack him when they are set

name: Lakshmipathy Balaji
strengths: 76 IPL wickets at 8.05 economy as a reliable domestic pacer who was a consistent contributor across many seasons
weaknesses: Modest international pedigree and not a genuine wicket-taker on good batting surfaces

name: Alfonso Thomas
strengths: Experienced South African seamer who contributed reliable economy and death-over wickets for multiple franchises
weaknesses: Limited pace by international standards but dependable economy and death-over discipline were consistently good

name: Jacob Duffy
strengths: New Zealand new-ball specialist with consistent powerplay quality who contributed usefully in 2026 IPL
weaknesses: Not a death-over specialist and batting is negligible to the team

name: Digvesh Rathi
strengths: Developing IPL leg-spinner with wicket-taking potential whose 2026 season showed real improvement
weaknesses: Still needs sustained seasons to confirm long-term T20 franchise quality

name: Dushmantha Chameera
strengths: Sri Lankan right-arm pace bowler who can contribute in all phases and generates decent pace
weaknesses: Economy is inconsistent and injury history has limited his IPL availability significantly

name: Dirk Nannes
strengths: 28 IPL wickets at 7.29 economy as a dual-passport left-arm quick who was one of the fastest in early IPL seasons
weaknesses: Short IPL career and batting minimal making him a pure specialist with limited all-round value

name: Riley Meredith
strengths: Australian rapid bowler who generates pace and can take death-over wickets with pace off a short length
weaknesses: Economy can be very expensive when rhythm is off and batting is negligible

name: Richard Gleeson
strengths: English new-ball specialist with late-career IPL return and consistent powerplay accuracy and movement
weaknesses: Minimal batting and declining at 38 which reduces his peak pace and effectiveness

name: Kuldeep Sen
strengths: Chhattisgarh right-arm pacer who contributes across phases and has decent IPL wicket-taking record
weaknesses: Not a premium specialist in any one phase and economy needs tightening at franchise level

name: Gurjapneet Singh
strengths: Left-arm pace option with limited IPL appearances and some domestic quality showing
weaknesses: Very limited senior experience and needs sustained franchise opportunities to develop

name: Manimaran Siddharth
strengths: Tamil Nadu left-arm spinner with consistent domestic record and useful T20 franchise economy
weaknesses: Limited IPL sample and needs more opportunities to show this quality at the top level

name: Jacob Bethell
strengths: Young English all-rounder with genuine two-way talent and exciting T20 upside including IPL promise
weaknesses: Still converting potential into sustained output and consistency across a full season is the challenge

name: Paul Collingwood
strengths: Solid CSK and KXIP all-rounder who brought tactical intelligence and dependable middle-order batting
weaknesses: Never the most explosive in any discipline — the glue-player archetype rather than a match-winning influence

name: Mahipal Lomror
strengths: Left-hand middle-order batter and part-time left-arm spinner who has contributed in multiple IPL seasons
weaknesses: Not yet a consistent performer and both departments are below elite franchise level

name: Deepak Hooda
strengths: Right-hand middle-order batter with consistent domestic IPL career and useful part-time medium contribution
weaknesses: Not exceptional in either department at franchise level and role has shifted between teams

name: Donovan Ferreira
strengths: South African keeper-finisher who scored 317 runs for RR in 2026 IPL with good lower-order strike rate
weaknesses: Small IPL sample and the batting output needs to be confirmed across more seasons at this level

name: Naman Dhir
strengths: Right-hand middle-order batter for MI with good IPL record who accumulates runs with tempo awareness
weaknesses: Power ceiling below specialist finishers and is best suited to role of bridging middle and death overs

name: Urvil Patel
strengths: Attacking keeper-opener from Gujarat who scored at over 200 SR for CSK in 2026 with big-hitting ability
weaknesses: Small sample and the ability to sustain such strike rates across a full season is unproven

name: Tejasvi Dahiya
strengths: Young right-hand middle-order batter with promising domestic track record and developing T20 franchise game
weaknesses: Very limited IPL outings and needs to establish a regular first-team role with sustained output

name: Srikar Bharat
strengths: Consistent domestic wicketkeeper-batter who has played for multiple IPL teams with solid if unspectacular output
weaknesses: Not a power-hitter and T20 batting needs more aggressive intent at the franchise level

name: Mukul Choudhary
strengths: Young right-hand batter who scored 170 runs for LSG in 2026 with decent strike rate and improving form
weaknesses: Very limited sample and needs extended franchise opportunities to establish consistent T20 quality

name: Karun Nair
strengths: Experienced right-hand batter with a strong domestic record who scored well for DC in 2026 including an 89
weaknesses: T20 power game is not exceptional and batting needs more consistent IPL output across full seasons

name: Swapnil Singh
strengths: Left-arm spinner and left-hand batter who contributed consistently in domestic cricket and IPL outings
weaknesses: Older player and both departments are below the very best IPL franchise-level performers

name: Will Sutherland
strengths: Australian bowling all-rounder whose developing credentials make him a viable T20 franchise option
weaknesses: Not at the elite level yet and both bowling economy and batting contribution need more consistency

name: Nathan Smith
strengths: New Zealand bowling all-rounder with solid T20 credentials and genuine two-way franchise value
weaknesses: Not yet established at the highest IPL level and both departments need more consistent output

name: Ben Dwarshuis
strengths: Australian left-arm death specialist with useful lower-order batting cameo ability and good T20 variations
weaknesses: Economy at death under high-pressure situations can spike and batting is not reliable

name: Mitchell Owen
strengths: Young Australian all-rounder who bats aggressively in lower-order and contributes useful pace bowling
weaknesses: IPL experience is very limited and both departments need further development at this level

name: Arshad Khan
strengths: Aggressive lower-order left-hand batter and left-arm pacer who contributes usefully in limited overs
weaknesses: IPL opportunities limited and neither department is at the elite franchise level consistently

name: Shivam Mavi
strengths: Young right-arm pacer who generates good pace and took useful powerplay wickets in early IPL career
weaknesses: Economy needs tightening at franchise level and sustained top-level performance across seasons needed

name: Manav Suthar
strengths: Young Gujarat left-arm spinner who has shown good control and economy in limited IPL appearances
weaknesses: Very young and needs more sustained franchise experience to confirm elite T20 spinner status
